keyPoints: ["Reduce everything to sine and cosine early","Pythagorean identities replace $1$ wherever convenient","Rationalizing numerators reveals hidden factors","Factoring out common terms exposes the target form"]
modelAnswer:
i. $(1-\sin^{2}\theta)\sec^{2}\theta=\cos^{2}\theta\cdot\frac{1}{\cos^{2}\theta}=1$.
ii. Multiply top and bottom by $(1-\sin\theta)$:
$\frac{(1-\sin\theta)^{2}}{1-\sin^{2}\theta}=\frac{(1-\sin\theta)^{2}}{\cos^{2}\theta}=(\sec\theta-\tan\theta)^{2}$.
iii. Rationalize inside the root by multiplying over $\frac{1-\cos\theta}{1-\cos\theta}$:
$\sqrt{\frac{(1-\cos)^{2}}{1-\cos^{2}}}=\frac{1-\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}=\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}$ using $(1-\cos)(1+\cos)=\sin^{2}$.
iv. Factor: $\frac{\sin\theta(1-2\sin^{2}\theta)}{\cos\theta(2\cos^{2}\theta-1)}=\frac{\sin\theta\cos2\theta}{\cos\theta\cos2\theta}=\tan\theta$.
v. $\sec^{2}+\operatorname{cosec}^{2}=\frac{\sin^{2}+\cos^{2}}{\sin^{2}\cos^{2}}=\sec^{2}\operatorname{cosec}^{2}$; taking the positive root,
$\sec\theta\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\tan\theta+\cot\theta$.
vi. $(\sec\theta-\tan\theta)(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)=\sec^{2}-\tan^{2}=1$, so the reciprocal claim holds.
vii. Difference of sides: $\sin^{2}-\sin^{4}=\sin^{2}\cos^{2}$ and $\cos^{4}-\cos^{2}=-\sin^{2}\cos^{2}$, so both sides are equal.
viii. Divide numerator and denominator by $\sin\theta$: each $\tan/\sin$ becomes $\sec$:
$\frac{\sec\theta+1}{\sec\theta-1}$.
ix. Shown in v: $\sec^{2}\theta+\operatorname{cosec}^{2}\theta=\frac{1}{\sin^{2}\cos^{2}}=\sec^{2}\theta\operatorname{cosec}^{2}\theta$.
x. With $a=\sin^{2}, b=\cos^{2}$: $a^{3}+b^{3}=(a+b)^{3}-3ab(a+b)=1-3\sin^{2}\theta\cos^{2}\theta$.
